title.zh: 卷280 列傳六十七 郎坦 朋春 萨布素 玛拉
title.en: Volume 280 Biographies 67: Lang Tan, Peng Chun, Sa Bu Su, Ma La
title.raw: 卷280 列傳六十七 郎坦 朋春 萨布素 玛拉

sentences.zh: 列傳六十七

translations.literal: Biographies 67
translations.idiomatic: Biography 67

sentences.zh: 郎坦朋春薩布素瑪拉

translations.literal: Lang Tan, Peng Chun, Sabsu, Ma La
translations.idiomatic: Lang Tan, Peng Chun, Sabsu, and Ma La

sentences.zh: 郎坦，瓜爾佳氏，滿洲正白旗人，內大臣吳拜子。

translations.literal: Lang Tan, of the Guwalgiya clan, was a Manchu of the Plain White Banner and son of the Inner Minister Wubai.
translations.idiomatic: Lang Tan, of the Guwalgiya clan, belonged to the Manchu Plain White Banner and was the son of Inner Minister Wubai.

sentences.zh: 年十四，授三等侍衛。

translations.literal: At age fourteen he was appointed a third-class bodyguard.
translations.idiomatic: At fourteen he received appointment as a third-class bodyguard.

sentences.zh: 順治六年，進二等。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Shunzhi he was promoted to second class.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 6 he was promoted to the second rank.

sentences.zh: 從端重親王博洛討叛將薑瓖，次渾源，圍城。

translations.literal: He followed Prince Duanzhong Bolo to suppress the rebel general Jiang Xiang, halted at Hunyuan, and besieged the city.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Prince Duanzhong Bolo against the rebel Jiang Xiang, camped at Hunyuan, and laid siege to the city.

sentences.zh: 賊渡濠來犯，郎坦射其酋，貫心，殪，遂敗賊。

translations.literal: When rebels crossed the moat to attack, Lang Tan shot their chief through the heart and killed him, and thus defeated the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels crossed the moat to attack; Lang Tan shot their leader through the heart and killed him, routing the enemy.

sentences.zh: 師還，進一等。

translations.literal: When the army returned he was promoted to first class.
translations.idiomatic: After the army returned he was promoted to first class.

sentences.zh: 八年，以吳拜附和內大臣洛什等獲罪，並奪郎坦官。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, because Wubai had joined Inner Minister Luoshi and others in an offense, Lang Tan's office was also stripped.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year Wubai was condemned for siding with Inner Minister Luoshi and others, and Lang Tan was stripped of his post as well.

sentences.zh: 尋復之。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward it was restored.
translations.idiomatic: Before long his office was restored.

sentences.zh: 康熙二年，代吳拜管佐領，遷護軍參領。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kangxi he replaced Wubai in managing an assistant banner command and was transferred to assistant commandant of the guards.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 2 he took over Wubai's assistant banner command and was made assistant commandant of the guards.

sentences.zh: 從定西將軍圖海討李自成餘黨李來亨等於茅麓山，深入賊巢，獲所置官十一。

translations.literal: He followed the Pacify-the-West General Tu Hai in campaigning against Li Zicheng's remnant Li Laiheng and others at Maolu Mountain, penetrated deep into the rebel nest, and captured eleven officials they had appointed.
translations.idiomatic: He served under Pacify-the-West General Tu Hai against Li Zicheng's remnant Li Laiheng at Maolu Mountain, penetrated the rebel stronghold, and seized eleven officials they had installed.

sentences.zh: 四年，襲一等精奇尼哈番。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he inherited a first-class jingqi niha fan.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he inherited a first-class baronetcy (jingqi niha fan).

sentences.zh: 十二年，京師有陳三道者，設壇以邪教惑眾，命郎坦與諸侍衛捕治。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year a man named Chen Sandao in the capital set up an altar and deluded the masses with heterodox teachings; Lang Tan and other bodyguards were ordered to arrest and punish him.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year a certain Chen Sandao in the capital used an altar and a heterodox cult to mislead the people; the court ordered Lang Tan and fellow bodyguards to seize and punish him.

sentences.zh: 十三年，命行邊，獲逋盜張飛腿等。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he was ordered to patrol the frontier and captured the fleeing bandit Zhang Feitui and others.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he was sent on frontier patrol and captured the fugitive Zhang Feitui and his gang.

sentences.zh: 擢正白旗蒙古副都統，調本旗滿洲。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Mongol deputy lieutenant-general of the Plain White Banner and transferred to the Manchu command of the same banner.
translations.idiomatic: He was raised to Mongol deputy lieutenant-general of the Plain White Banner, then shifted to the banner's Manchu command.

sentences.zh: 順治中，俄羅斯東部人犯黑龍江邊境，時稱為羅剎。

translations.literal: During Shunzhi, people from eastern Russia violated the Amur frontier and were at the time called Luocha.
translations.idiomatic: Under Shunzhi, Russians from the east raided the Amur borderlands and were then called Luocha.

sentences.zh: 九年，駐防寧古塔章京海塞遣捕牲翼長希福率兵與戰，師敗績。

translations.literal: In the ninth year the garrison commander of Ningguta, Haise, sent the livestock-capture wing chief Xifu to lead troops against them; the army suffered defeat.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year Ningguta commander Haise sent wing chief Xifu of the hunting detachment with troops to fight them and was defeated.

sentences.zh: 世祖命誅海塞，鞭希福百，仍駐寧古塔。

translations.literal: The Shunzhi Emperor ordered Haise executed, Xifu flogged one hundred strokes, and garrison duty at Ningguta continued.
translations.idiomatic: Shunzhi ordered Haise put to death, Xifu given a hundred lashes, and the Ningguta garrison maintained.

sentences.zh: 十一年，固山額真明安達里率師討之，敗敵黑龍江。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year gushen ejen Mingandali led an army against them and defeated the enemy on the Amur.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year banner commander Mingandali took an army against them and beat the foe on the Amur.

sentences.zh: 羅剎未大創，复侵入精奇里江諸處。

translations.literal: The Russians were not badly crippled and again invaded the regions along the Jingqili River.
translations.idiomatic: The Russians were not broken decisively and again pushed into the Jingqili River country.

sentences.zh: 上命大理寺卿明愛等諭令撤回，遷延不即去，據雅克薩城，於其旁耕種漁獵；

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Minister of Justice Ming Ai and others to instruct them to withdraw; they delayed and did not leave at once, held Albazin, and farmed and fished beside it;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Minister of Justice Ming Ai and others to order them back; they lingered, would not leave promptly, seized Albazin, and planted and fished around it;

sentences.zh: 又過牛滿、恆滾，侵擾索倫、赫哲、飛牙喀、奇勒爾諸部。

translations.literal: they also crossed the Nioman and Henggun, harassing the Solon, Hezhe, Feiyaka, Qiler, and other tribes.
translations.idiomatic: they crossed the Nioman and Henggun as well, raiding the Solon, Hezhe, Feiyaka, Qiler, and other peoples.

sentences.zh: 二十一年秋，遣郎坦及副都統朋春等率兵往索倫。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the twenty-first year Lang Tan and Deputy Lieutenant-General Peng Chun and others were sent with troops to the Solon region.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn of Kangxi 21 the court dispatched Lang Tan, Deputy Lieutenant-General Peng Chun, and others with troops toward Solon.

sentences.zh: 比行，諭曰：「羅剎犯我境，恃雅克薩城為巢穴，歷年已久，殺掠不已。

translations.literal: Before they set out, he was instructed: "The Russians violate our borders, relying on Albazin as their nest; for many years they have not ceased killing and plundering.
translations.idiomatic: On the eve of departure he was told: "The Russians invade our territory, using Albazin as their lair; year after year they kill and plunder without end.

sentences.zh: 爾等至達呼爾、索倫，遣人往諭以來捕鹿。

translations.literal: When you reach Dahur and Solon, send men to summon them on the pretext of coming to hunt deer.
translations.idiomatic: When you reach the Dahur and Solon, send envoys inviting them to come hunt deer.

sentences.zh: 因詳視陸路遠近，沿黑龍江行圍，迳薄雅克薩城，勘其形勢。

translations.literal: Thereby examine carefully the distances overland, conduct a hunting drive along the Amur, press straight upon Albazin, and survey its situation.
translations.idiomatic: Use that occasion to measure overland distances in detail, run a battue along the Amur, close on Albazin directly, and reconnoiter its defenses.

sentences.zh: 度羅剎不敢出戰，如出戰，姑勿交鋒，但率剎引退。

translations.literal: Judge that the Russians will not dare give battle; if they do fight, for the moment do not engage—only lead them to withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: Expect the Russians not to dare fight; if they do, for now do not clash—only draw them off.

sentences.zh: 朕別有區畫。

translations.literal: I have other plans.
translations.idiomatic: I have a separate design."

sentences.zh: 」賜御用裘服、弓矢以行。

translations.literal: " He was granted imperial fur garments, bow and arrows, and sent on his way.
translations.idiomatic: He was given imperial furs, bow, and arrows for the journey.

sentences.zh: 及冬，郎坦等還京師，疏言：「羅剎久踞雅克薩，恃有木城。

translations.literal: When winter came Lang Tan and the others returned to the capital and memorialized: "The Russians have long held Albazin, relying on its wooden fort.
translations.idiomatic: By winter Lang Tan's party was back in Beijing and reported: "The Luocha have entrenched themselves at Albazin behind a timber palisade.

sentences.zh: 若發兵三千，與紅衣砲二十，即可攻取。

translations.literal: If three thousand troops are sent with twenty red-coated cannon, it can be taken.
translations.idiomatic: Send three thousand men and twenty red-coated guns and it can be taken."

sentences.zh: 陸行自興安嶺以往，林木叢雜，冬雪堅冰，夏雨泥淖，惟輕裝可行。

translations.literal: Going by land from the Greater Khingan range, the woods are dense; winter brings hard ice, summer rains turn the ground to mud—only light equipment can pass.
translations.idiomatic: The land route from the Greater Khingan is thick forest; in winter the snow freezes solid, in summer rain turns the trails to mire—only light columns can march.

sentences.zh: 自雅克薩還至愛滹城，於黑龍江順流行船，僅須半月，逆流行船，約須三月，倍於陸行，期於運糧餉、軍器、輜重為便。

translations.literal: From Albazin back to Aihui City, going downstream on the Amur by boat takes only half a month; going upstream takes about three months, twice the land march, but is better for hauling grain, weapons, and baggage.
translations.idiomatic: From Albazin to Aihui City, a downstream Amur voyage needs barely half a month; upstream needs roughly three months—double the land time—but suits grain, ordnance, and stores.

sentences.zh: 現有大船四十、小船二十六，宜增造小船五十餘應用。

translations.literal: There are now forty large boats and twenty-six small ones; more than fifty small boats should be built for use.
translations.idiomatic: We now have forty large junks and twenty-six small ones; fifty-odd more small craft should be built."

sentences.zh: 」上諭曰：「郎坦等奏攻取羅剎甚易，朕亦以為然。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Lang Tan and the others report that taking the Russians is very easy, and I too think so.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied: "Lang Tan says the Russians are easy to crush, and I agree.

sentences.zh: 第兵非善事，宜暫停攻取。

translations.literal: Yet war is no small matter; the attack should be paused for now.
translations.idiomatic: But war is no light thing—hold off the assault for the present.

sentences.zh: 調烏拉、寧古塔兵千五百人，並製造船艦，發紅衣砲、鳥槍教之演習。

translations.literal: Mobilize fifteen hundred troops from Ula and Ningguta, build warships, and issue red-coated cannon and muskets to drill them.
translations.idiomatic: Raise fifteen hundred men from Ula and Ningguta, build ships, issue red-coated guns and muskets, and drill them.

sentences.zh: 於愛琿、呼瑪爾二地建木城，與之對壘，相機舉行。

translations.literal: Build wooden forts at Aihui and Humar to face them and strike when the moment is right.
translations.idiomatic: Erect wooden forts at Aihui and Humar to confront them and act when opportunity offers.

sentences.zh: 所需軍糧，取諸科爾沁十旗及錫伯、烏拉官屯，約得一萬二千石，可支三年。

translations.literal: Army grain should be drawn from the ten Khorchin banners and the official farms of Xibe and Ula, about twelve thousand shi, enough for three years.
translations.idiomatic: Provisions can come from the ten Khorchin banners plus Xibe and Ula state farms—about twelve thousand shi, enough for three years.

sentences.zh: 愛琿城距索倫五宿可至，其間設一驛。

translations.literal: Aihui City is five days' march from Solon; set a post station between.
translations.idiomatic: Aihui lies five marches from Solon; place a courier station en route.

sentences.zh: 俟我兵將至精奇里烏拉，令索倫供牛羊。

translations.literal: When our troops are about to reach Jingqili Ula, have the Solon supply cattle and sheep.
translations.idiomatic: When our force nears Jingqili Ula, let Solon furnish cattle and sheep.

sentences.zh: 如此，則羅剎不得納我逋逃，而彼之逋逃且絡繹來歸，自不能久存矣。

translations.literal: Thus the Russians cannot shelter our fugitives, while their own deserters will come in streams and they cannot long endure."
translations.idiomatic: Then the Russians cannot harbor our runaways, their own fugitives will stream to us, and they cannot last long."

sentences.zh: 」尋擢郎坦前鋒統領。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Lang Tan was promoted to vanguard commander.
translations.idiomatic: Lang Tan was soon made vanguard commander.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，命與黑龍江將軍薩布素會議，駐兵額蘇哩。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year he was ordered to confer with Heilongjiang General Sabsu and garrison troops at Esuri.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 22 he was told to consult Heilongjiang general Sabsu and station troops at Esuri.

sentences.zh: 事還，奏額蘇哩七月即經霜雪，宜乘春和，以寧古塔兵分為三班，更番戍守。

translations.literal: When the mission ended he memorialized that Esuri sees frost and snow as early as the seventh month and that, while spring is mild, Ningguta troops should be divided into three shifts for rotating garrison duty.
translations.idiomatic: On return he noted Esuri frosts by the seventh month; only spring is mild—split Ningguta's men into three reliefs, he urged.

sentences.zh: 上以更番戍守非久長策，不允。

translations.literal: The emperor said rotating garrison was no long-term policy and did not approve.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor judged rotation no lasting policy and refused.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，甄別八旗管兵官，罷郎坦前鋒統領，以世職隨旗行走。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year, in the review of Eight Banner commanders, Lang Tan was removed as vanguard commander and served by hereditary rank within his banner.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 23, during the review of banner officers, Lang Tan lost the vanguard command and kept only his hereditary title with the banner.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，命都統朋春率師徵羅剎，郎坦以副都統銜隨徵。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year Commander-in-Chief Peng Chun was ordered to campaign against the Russians; Lang Tan followed as deputy lieutenant-general.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 24 Commander Peng Chun was sent against the Russians; Lang Tan went as acting deputy lieutenant-general.

sentences.zh: 師薄雅克薩城，羅剎酋額里克舍請降，郎坦宣詔宥其罪，引眾徙去，毀木城。

translations.literal: When the army reached Albazin the Russian chief Yerikexie asked to surrender; Lang Tan proclaimed the edict pardoning his crime, led the people away, and destroyed the wooden fort.
translations.idiomatic: At Albazin the Russian leader Yerikexie sued for peace; Lang Tan read the amnesty, moved the people out, and razed the timber fort.

sentences.zh: 是冬羅剎復來，踞雅克薩築城。

translations.literal: That winter the Russians came again and reoccupied Albazin, building a fort.
translations.idiomatic: That winter the Russians returned, reoccupied Albazin, and rebuilt fortifications.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，命郎坦偕副都統班達爾沙攜紅衣砲，率藤牌兵百人，往會將軍薩布素進兵。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year Lang Tan was ordered to go with Deputy Lieutenant-General Bandarsha, bringing red-coated cannon and a hundred rattan-shield troops, to join General Sabsu's advance.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 25 Lang Tan, with Deputy Lieutenant-General Bandarsha, red-coated guns, and a hundred rattan-shield men, was sent to reinforce General Sabsu.

sentences.zh: 上以郎坦諳悉地勢，即令參贊軍務。

translations.literal: Because Lang Tan knew the terrain well, he was at once made a staff adviser on military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing the country, Lang Tan was immediately named a campaign adviser.

sentences.zh: 六月，薄其城，鑿壕築壘，賊出拒，擊敗之，斬額里克舍。

translations.literal: In the sixth month they pressed the city, dug trenches and built ramparts; the enemy came out to resist and was defeated; Yerikexie was beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month they closed on the town, dug trenches and breastworks; the garrison sallied, was beaten, and Yerikexie was killed.

sentences.zh: 尋，俄羅斯察罕汗上書請釋雅克薩圍，上許之，令郎坦撤軍，還駐寧古塔。

translations.literal: Soon the Russian Tsagan Khan wrote asking that the siege of Albazin be lifted; the emperor agreed and ordered Lang Tan to withdraw the army and return to garrison Ningguta.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Russia's Tsagan Khan asked to lift the siege; the emperor consented and ordered Lang Tan back to Ningguta.

sentences.zh: 尋擢正白旗蒙古都統。

translations.literal: He was soon promoted to Mongol lieutenant-general of the Plain White Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly after he became Mongol lieutenant-general of the Plain White Banner.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，上遣內大臣索額圖等與俄羅斯使人費耀多囉等會於尼布楚，立約定界，命郎坦與議，乃毀所築城徙去。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year the emperor sent Inner Minister Songgotu and others to meet the Russian envoy Feodor at Nerchinsk to fix the border; Lang Tan took part in the talks, and the forts they had built were destroyed and the people moved away.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 28 Inner Minister Songgotu met the Russian envoy Feodor at Nerchinsk to delimit the frontier; Lang Tan joined the negotiations, after which the Russian posts were demolished and the settlers removed.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，古北口外盜起，命郎坦偕侍衛赫濟爾亨等督兵捕剿，盡殲之。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year bandits rose outside Gubeikou; Lang Tan was ordered with Bodyguard Hejierheng and others to supervise troops in pursuit and exterminated them.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 29 brigands appeared beyond Gubeikou; Lang Tan, with Bodyguard Hejierheng and others, led pursuit troops and wiped them out.

sentences.zh: 三十一年，噶爾丹侵喀爾喀部，擾及邊境，授郎坦安北將軍，率師駐大同。

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year Galdan invaded the Khalkha and disturbed the frontier; Lang Tan was made Pacify-the-North General and led troops to garrison Datong.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 31 Galdan struck the Khalkha and harassed the border; Lang Tan was named Pacify-the-North General and encamped at Datong.

sentences.zh: 疏請出邊駐喀喇穆倫偵寇，詔暫駐歸化城。

translations.literal: He memorialized asking to advance beyond the border and garrison Karamuren to watch the enemy; he was ordered to remain temporarily at Guihua City.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to move forward to Karamuren to scout; the court told him to stay at Guihua City for the time being.

sentences.zh: 尋擢領侍衛內大臣，兼火器營總管，列議政大臣。

translations.literal: He was soon promoted to chief bodyguard of the inner court, concurrently superintendent of the Firearms Corps, and seated among the deliberating ministers.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon chief inner bodyguard, head of the Firearms Corps, and a deliberating minister.

sentences.zh: 三十二年，授昭武將軍，率師駐甘州。

translations.literal: In the thirty-second year he was made General Who Manifests Martiality and led troops to garrison Ganzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 32 he became General Who Manifests Martiality and took the army to Ganzhou.

sentences.zh: 三十三年，移駐寧夏，與甘肅提督孫思克分道偵寇。

translations.literal: In the thirty-third year he shifted to Ningxia and, with Gansu provincial military commissioner Sun Sike, divided routes to scout the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 33 he moved to Ningxia and, with Gansu commissioner Sun Sike, patrolled on separate lines.

sentences.zh: 上聞噶爾丹將逼圖拉，命郎坦移兵禦剿，以圖拉無警，引還。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard Galdan was about to threaten Tula, Lang Tan was ordered to move troops to intercept; as Tula was unthreatened, he led them back.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing Galdan might threaten Tula, the emperor ordered Lang Tan forward; finding Tula secure, he withdrew.

sentences.zh: 仍任領侍衛內大臣，列議政如故。

translations.literal: He again served as chief bodyguard of the inner court and deliberating minister as before.
translations.idiomatic: He resumed his posts as chief bodyguard and deliberating minister.

sentences.zh: 三十四年，往盛京巡閱邊隘，還入塞，疾劇，遣太醫馳驛往視。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fourth year he went to Shengjing to inspect frontier passes; on re-entering the passes he fell gravely ill, and an imperial physician was sent post-haste to examine him.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 34 he inspected the Shengjing frontier; re-entering the Great Wall he grew desperately ill, and a court physician was rushed to him.

sentences.zh: 尋卒，賜祭葬。

translations.literal: He soon died and was granted funeral rites.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon after; the court granted funeral honors.

sentences.zh: 朋春，棟鄂氏，滿洲正紅旗人，何和禮四世孫。

translations.literal: Peng Chun, of the Donggo clan, was a Manchu of the Plain Red Banner and fourth-generation descendant of Heheli.
translations.idiomatic: Peng Chun, of the Donggo clan, belonged to the Manchu Plain Red Banner and was Heheli's great-great-grandson.

sentences.zh: 何和禮子和碩圖，進爵三等公；

translations.literal: Heheli's son Hosotu was raised to third-class duke;
translations.idiomatic: Heheli's son Hosotu was ennobled a third-class duke;

sentences.zh: 子何爾本、哲爾本、蘇布遞襲，至袞布，以恩詔進一等。

translations.literal: sons He'erben, Zhe'erben, and Subudi inherited in turn, down to Gunbu, who was advanced to first class by grace edict.
translations.idiomatic: his sons He'erben, Zhe'erben, and Subudi inherited in succession until Gunbu, promoted to first class by imperial grace.

sentences.zh: 朋春，哲爾本子也，順治九年，襲封。

translations.literal: Peng Chun was son of Zhe'erben and inherited the title in the ninth year of Shunzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Peng Chun was Zhe'erben's son and inherited in Shunzhi 9.

sentences.zh: 康熙十五年，加太子太保，授正紅旗蒙古副都統，調本旗滿洲。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Kangxi he was made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and appointed Mongol deputy lieutenant-general of the Plain Red Banner, then transferred to the Manchu command.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 15 he became Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, Mongol deputy lieutenant-general of the Plain Red Banner, then shifted to its Manchu wing.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，偕郎坦率兵至黑龍江覘羅剎形勢，賜御用裘服、弓矢。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year, together with Lang Tan, he led troops to the Amur to reconnoiter the Russians and was granted imperial fur garments, bow, and arrows.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 21 he joined Lang Tan on the Amur reconnaissance of the Russians and received imperial furs, bow, and arrows.

sentences.zh: 與郎坦還奏，上命寧古塔將軍巴海、副都統薩布素，建木城於黑龍江、呼瑪爾，調取所部兵一千五百人往駐焉。

translations.literal: When he and Lang Tan returned and reported, the emperor ordered Ningguta General Bahai and Deputy Lieutenant-General Sabsu to build wooden forts on the Amur and at Humar and to move fifteen hundred of their troops there to garrison.
translations.idiomatic: On their return the emperor told Ningguta general Bahai and deputy Sabsu to erect wooden forts on the Amur and at Humar and station fifteen hundred men there.

sentences.zh: 又命尚書伊桑阿赴寧古塔督造戰船。

translations.literal: He also ordered Minister Yisangga to go to Ningguta to supervise construction of warships.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Yisangga was also sent to Ningguta to oversee warship building.

sentences.zh: 尋擢朋春正紅旗滿洲副都統。

translations.literal: Peng Chun was soon promoted to Manchu deputy lieutenant-general of the Plain Red Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Peng Chun soon became Manchu deputy lieutenant-general of the Plain Red Banner.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，詔選八旗及安置山東、河南、山西三省福建投誠藤牌兵，付左都督何祐率赴盛京，命朋春統之，進剿羅剎，以副都統班達爾沙、副都統銜瑪拉、鑾儀使建義侯林興珠、護軍統領佟寶參贊軍務，祐、興珠皆鄭氏將來降者也。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year an edict selected troops from the Eight Banners and Fujian surrender rattan-shield soldiers settled in Shandong, Henan, and Shanxi, placed under Left Commissioner He You to proceed to Shengjing; Peng Chun was ordered to command them in the campaign against the Russians, with Deputy Lieutenant-General Bandarsha, acting deputy Ma La, Ceremonial Commissioner and Jianyi Marquis Lin Xingzhu, and Guards Commander Tong Bao as staff advisers—He You and Lin Xingzhu were both generals who had surrendered from Zheng Chenggong's forces.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 24 the court picked Eight Banner troops plus Fujian rattan-shield levies settled in Shandong, Henan, and Shanxi, gave them to Left Commissioner He You for Shengjing, and put Peng Chun in command against the Russians with Bandarsha, acting deputy Ma La, Ceremonial Commissioner Lin Xingzhu (Marquis Jianyi), and Guards Commander Tong Bao on his staff—He You and Lin Xingzhu were Zheng Chenggong's former officers.

sentences.zh: 師既行，上遣侍衛關保至黑龍江傳諭曰：「兵凶戰危，朕以仁治天下，素不嗜殺。

translations.literal: After the army marched the emperor sent Bodyguard Guanbao to the Amur with instructions: "War is perilous; I govern the realm with benevolence and do not delight in killing.
translations.idiomatic: As the army marched, Bodyguard Guanbao carried the emperor's word to the Amur: "War is cruel; I rule by benevolence and do not love bloodshed.

sentences.zh: 以我兵馬精強，器械堅利，羅剎勢不能敵，必獻地歸誠。

translations.literal: With our troops skilled and our weapons strong, the Russians cannot stand against us and will surely yield land and submit.
translations.idiomatic: Our men are seasoned and our arms superior—the Russians cannot resist and will surrender territory.

sentences.zh: 爾時勿殺一人，俾還故土，宣朕柔遠至意。

translations.literal: When that time comes kill no one; let them return to their homeland and proclaim my far-reaching gentleness."
translations.idiomatic: When that hour comes, kill none; send them home and proclaim my care for distant peoples."

sentences.zh: 」五月，師薄雅克薩城，遣人諭降，不從。

translations.literal: In the fifth month the army reached Albazin and sent men to summon surrender; they would not submit.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month the force reached Albazin and called on them to yield; they refused.

sentences.zh: 分水陸兵為兩路，列營夾攻，复移紅衣砲於前，積薪城下，示將焚焉。

translations.literal: Land and river forces were divided into two columns, camps were set on both sides for a pincer attack, red-coated cannon were moved forward, and firewood was piled at the foot of the wall to show it would be burned.
translations.idiomatic: Troops split by land and water, camps closed in from both sides, red-coated guns were advanced, and brush was heaped against the wall as if to burn it.

sentences.zh: 羅剎頭目額里克舍詣軍前乞降，乃宥其罪，釋還俘虜，額里克舍引六百餘人徙去，毀木城，以歸附巴什裡等四十五戶及被掠索倫、達呼爾百餘戶安插內地。

translations.literal: The Russian leader Yerikexie came before the army to beg mercy; his crime was pardoned, captives were released, Yerikexie led more than six hundred people away, the wooden fort was destroyed, and forty-five households of the Bashiri and more than a hundred Solon and Dahur households seized by the enemy were resettled inland.
translations.idiomatic: Russian chief Yerikexie came to beg pardon; the court forgave him, freed prisoners, and let him withdraw six hundred-odd followers while the timber fort was razed; forty-five Bashiri households and over a hundred seized Solon and Dahur families were settled inland.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，厄魯特與喀爾喀構釁，命裕親王福全為撫遠大將軍，出邊剿噶爾丹，以朋春與都統蘇努參贊軍務。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year the Eleuths and Khalkha quarreled; Prince Fuquan was made Pacify-the-Distant Grand General to campaign against Galdan beyond the border, with Peng Chun and Commander Sunu as staff advisers.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 29 Eleuths and Khalkha clashed; Prince Fuquan became Pacify-the-Distant Grand General against Galdan, with Peng Chun and Sunu advising.

sentences.zh: 蘇努率左翼，朋春率右翼，至烏闌布通。

translations.literal: Sunu led the left wing and Peng Chun the right, advancing to Ulan Butung.
translations.idiomatic: Sunu took the left, Peng Chun the right, to Ulan Butung.

sentences.zh: 噶爾丹依山列陣，朋春所部為泥淖所阻，蘇努督兵衝擊，大破之。

translations.literal: Galdan drew up his array along the hills; Peng Chun's wing was blocked by mud; Sunu led troops in a charge and broke them utterly.
translations.idiomatic: Galdan formed on the hills; Peng Chun's wing bogged in marsh; Sunu charged and routed them.

sentences.zh: 噶爾丹偽乞和，夜自大磧山遁走。

translations.literal: Galdan falsely sued for peace and at night fled over Great Ditch Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Galdan feigned peace and fled by night over Great Ditch Mountain.

sentences.zh: 部議朋春坐奪官，上命寬之，降級留任。

translations.literal: The ministry proposed stripping Peng Chun of office; the emperor ordered leniency and reduced his rank while retaining him in post.
translations.idiomatic: The Board urged dismissal; the emperor was lenient, demoted him, and kept him on duty.

sentences.zh: 三十一年，命解職赴西路軍前管隊。

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year he was ordered to resign and go to the western army to manage a detachment.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 31 he was relieved and sent to the western front to command a column.

sentences.zh: 三十五年，复授正紅旗蒙古都統。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fifth year he was again made Mongol lieutenant-general of the Plain Red Banner.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 35 he again became Mongol lieutenant-general of the Plain Red Banner.

sentences.zh: 旋以費揚古為撫遠大將軍，朋春仍參贊軍務，出西路，破噶爾丹於昭莫多。

translations.literal: Soon Feiyanggu became Pacify-the-Distant Grand General; Peng Chun again served on his staff, took the western route, and defeated Galdan at Jao Modo.
translations.idiomatic: When Feiyanggu became grand general, Peng Chun again advised him, marched the western route, and helped crush Galdan at Jao Modo.

sentences.zh: 師還，以本隊護軍驍騎十八人戰死未收其骸，下部議。

translations.literal: When the army returned, eighteen brave guards of his command who died in battle had not had their bodies recovered; the matter was referred to the ministry for discussion.
translations.idiomatic: On return, eighteen of his guards killed in battle lay unburied; the case went to the Board.

sentences.zh: 以師有功，免罪，仍錄戰績，增註敕書。

translations.literal: Because the campaign had merit, punishment was waived, battle honors were still recorded, and the patent of appointment was augmented.
translations.idiomatic: Because the campaign succeeded, he was spared punishment, his battle record kept, and his patent enlarged.

sentences.zh: 三十八年，因病解職。

translations.literal: In the thirty-eighth year he resigned on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 38 illness forced his resignation.

sentences.zh: 尋卒。

translations.literal: He soon died.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon after.

sentences.zh: 子增壽，改襲三等公。

translations.literal: His son Zengshou changed inheritance to third-class duke.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zengshou inherited as a third-class duke.

sentences.zh: 薩布素，富察氏，滿洲鑲黃旗人。

translations.literal: Sabsu, of the Fuca clan, was a Manchu of the Bordered Yellow Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Sabsu, of the Fuca clan, belonged to the Manchu Bordered Yellow Banner.

sentences.zh: 四世祖充順巴本，以勇力聞，世為岳克通鄂城長。

translations.literal: His fourth-generation ancestor Chongshun Baben was famed for strength and for generations was chief of Yueketong'e City.
translations.idiomatic: Four generations back Chongshun Baben was renowned for valor; his line long ruled Yueketong'e City.

sentences.zh: 太祖時，其後人哈木都率所部來歸，屯吉林，遂家焉。

translations.literal: In the time of Taizu his descendant Hamudu led his people to submit, settled at Jilin, and made it their home.
translations.idiomatic: Under Taizu, descendant Hamudu brought his people in, settled in Jilin, and the family remained there.

sentences.zh: 薩布素自領催授驍騎校，遷協領。

translations.literal: Sabsu himself held a company command, was promoted to assistant commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Sabsu rose from company commander to assistant commandant.

sentences.zh: 康熙十六年，聖祖遣內大臣覺羅武默訥等瞻禮長白山，至吉林，欲得識路者導引。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year of Kangxi the Sacred Ancestor sent Inner Minister Aisin Gioro Wumune and others to pay homage at Mount Changbai; reaching Jilin they wished for a guide who knew the route.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 16 the emperor sent Inner Minister Wumune and others to worship at Mount Changbai; at Jilin they needed a pathfinder.

sentences.zh: 寧古塔將軍巴海令薩布素率兵二百，攜三月糧以從。

translations.literal: Ningguta General Bahai ordered Sabsu to lead two hundred troops with three months' grain to follow.
translations.idiomatic: Ningguta general Bahai told Sabsu to take two hundred men and three months' provisions.

sentences.zh: 水陸行，至長白山麓，成禮而還，事具武默訥傳。

translations.literal: Going by land and water they reached the foot of Mount Changbai, performed the rites, and returned; the affair is recorded in Wumune's biography.
translations.idiomatic: They went by land and water to the mountain's foot, completed the rites, and returned—the full account is in Wumune's biography.

sentences.zh: 十七年，授薩布素寧古塔副都統。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year Sabsu was appointed Ningguta deputy lieutenant-general.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 17 he became Ningguta deputy lieutenant-general.

sentences.zh: 羅剎據雅克薩，二十一年，詔率兵偕郎坦等勘視雅克薩城形勢，並往視自額蘇哩至黑龍江及通寧古塔水陸道。

translations.literal: The Russians held Albazin; in the twenty-first year he was ordered to lead troops with Lang Tan and others to survey Albazin's defenses and also to examine the land and water routes from Esuri to the Amur and on to Ningguta.
translations.idiomatic: Russians held Albazin; in Kangxi 21 he was told to join Lang Tan in reconnoitering Albazin and the Esuri–Amur–Ningguta routes by land and water.

sentences.zh: 尋郎坦還奏羅剎可圖狀，命建木城於黑龍江、呼瑪爾兩地，以巴海與薩布素統寧古塔兵千五百人往駐，造船備砲。

translations.literal: Soon Lang Tan returned and reported that the Russians could be dealt with; wooden forts were ordered built on the Amur and at Humar, with Bahai and Sabsu commanding fifteen hundred Ningguta troops to garrison there, build ships, and prepare cannon.
translations.idiomatic: When Lang Tan reported the Russians could be taken, the court ordered wooden forts on the Amur and at Humar; Bahai and Sabsu were to station fifteen hundred Ningguta men there, build ships, and ready guns.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，疏言：「黑龍江、呼瑪爾距雅克薩尚遠，若駐兵兩處，則勢分道阻，且過雅克薩有尼布楚等城。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year he memorialized: "The Amur and Humar are still far from Albazin; if troops garrison both places the force is divided and the route blocked, and beyond Albazin lie Nerchinsk and other towns.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 22 he argued: "Aihui and Humar lie too far from Albazin—split garrisons divide our strength and block the road, while beyond Albazin stand Nerchinsk and other Russian posts.

sentences.zh: 羅剎倘水陸運糧，增兵救援，更難為計。

translations.literal: If the Russians transport grain by land and water and send reinforcements, it will be still harder to manage.
translations.idiomatic: If they supply by river and road and reinforce, our task grows harder still.

sentences.zh: 宜乘其積貯未備，速行征剿。

translations.literal: We should strike while their stores are not yet ready and campaign swiftly.
translations.idiomatic: Strike before their stores are full—move quickly.

sentences.zh: 俟造船畢，度七月初旬能抵雅克薩，即統兵直薄城下。

translations.literal: When shipbuilding is finished, estimating that by early the seventh month we can reach Albazin, lead the army straight to the foot of the wall."
translations.idiomatic: When the fleet is ready—by early seventh month we can reach Albazin—drive straight to the walls."

sentences.zh: 」疏下王大臣議，如所請，上不許。

translations.literal: The memorial was sent to the princes and ministers for deliberation; they approved as requested, but the emperor did not consent.
translations.idiomatic: The princes endorsed his plan; the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 尋命巴海留守吉林，以薩布素偕寧古塔副都統瓦禮祜率兵駐額蘇哩。

translations.literal: He was soon ordered to have Bahai remain at Jilin while Sabsu, with Ningguta Deputy Lieutenant-General Walihu, led troops to garrison Esuri.
translations.idiomatic: Bahai was left at Jilin; Sabsu and deputy Walihu took the army to Esuri.

sentences.zh: 額蘇哩在黑龍江、呼瑪爾之間，為進攻雅克薩要地，有田隴舊跡。

translations.literal: Esuri lies between the Amur and Humar and is the key point for attacking Albazin; there are traces of old fields.
translations.idiomatic: Esuri, between the Amur and Humar, is the choke point for Albazin and still shows old field ridges.

sentences.zh: 薩布素因移達呼爾防兵五百人赴其地耕種，並請調寧古塔兵三千更番戍守。

translations.literal: Sabsu therefore moved five hundred Dahur garrison troops there to farm and asked that three thousand Ningguta troops be rotated in shifts for garrison duty.
translations.idiomatic: Sabsu shifted five hundred Dahur guards to farm there and asked for three thousand Ningguta men in rotating reliefs.

sentences.zh: 上念兵丁更戍勞苦，命在黑龍江建城，備攻具，設斥堠，計程置驛，運糧積貯，設將軍、副都統領之。

translations.literal: The emperor, mindful of the hardship of rotating garrisons, ordered a city built on the Amur, attack equipment prepared, watch posts set, post stations placed by measured stages, grain transported and stored, and a general and deputy lieutenant-general appointed to command.
translations.idiomatic: Pitying rotating garrisons, the emperor ordered an Amur fortress, siege gear, watch posts, courier stations, grain depots, and a general's command.

sentences.zh: 擢薩布素為黑龍江將軍，招撫羅剎降人，授以官職，更令轉相招撫。

translations.literal: Sabsu was promoted to Heilongjiang general, won over surrendered Russians, gave them offices, and ordered them to win others in turn.
translations.idiomatic: Sabsu became Heilongjiang general, enrolled Russian defectors in office, and set them to recruit others.

sentences.zh: 上命都統瓦山、侍郎果丕與薩布素議師期，薩布素請以來年四月水陸並進，攻雅克薩城，不克，則刈其田禾。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Commander Walishan and Vice Minister Guobi to discuss campaign timing with Sabsu; Sabsu asked that in the fourth month of the coming year land and river forces advance together against Albazin, and if it was not taken, cut their standing grain.
translations.idiomatic: Commander Walishan and Vice Minister Guobi were sent to fix the campaign date; Sabsu proposed a joint land–river assault next fourth month, cutting the fields if Albazin held.

sentences.zh: 上謂攻羅剎當期必克，倘謀事草率，將益肆猖狂。

translations.literal: The emperor said that attacking the Russians must be timed for certain victory; if planning were rash they would grow still more arrogant.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor warned that war on the Russians must promise victory—rash plans would only embolden them.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，以朋春等統兵進攻，薩布素會師，克雅克薩城，乃命薩布素移駐墨爾根，建城防禦。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year Peng Chun and others commanded the advance; Sabsu joined forces, took Albazin, and was then ordered to shift garrison to Merjen and build a city for defense.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 24 Peng Chun led the assault; Sabsu joined, took Albazin, then moved to Merjen to build defenses.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，疏言羅剎复踞雅克薩，請督修戰艦，俟冰泮進剿。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year he memorialized that the Russians had again seized Albazin and asked to supervise repair of warships and campaign when the ice broke.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 25 he reported Russians back at Albazin and asked to ready the fleet for a spring offensive.

sentences.zh: 上遣郎中滿丕往诇得實，乃命薩布素暫停墨爾根兵丁遷移家口，速修戰監，率寧古塔兵二千人往攻。

translations.literal: The emperor sent Director Manpi to reconnoiter and verify; then ordered Sabsu to pause moving families out of Merjen, repair warships swiftly, and lead two thousand Ningguta troops to attack.
translations.idiomatic: Director Manpi confirmed the report; Sabsu was told to halt family removals from Merjen, finish the fleet, and take two thousand Ningguta men.

sentences.zh: 又命郎坦、班達爾沙會師，抵雅克薩城。

translations.literal: Lang Tan and Bandarsha were also ordered to join forces and reach Albazin.
translations.idiomatic: Lang Tan and Bandarsha were ordered to unite on Albazin.

sentences.zh: 城西瀕江，薩布素令於城三面掘壕築壘為長圍，對江駐水師，未冰時泊舟東西岸，截尼布楚援兵，冰時藏舟上流汊港內；

translations.literal: The city's west adjoins the river; Sabsu ordered trenches and ramparts dug on three sides for a long encirclement and stationed the river force opposite; before ice, boats moored on both banks to cut Nerchinsk relief, and when frozen boats were hidden in upstream creeks;
translations.idiomatic: The west wall hugs the river; Sabsu ringed three land faces with trenches and breastworks, posted the flotilla opposite, kept boats on both banks before freeze-up to block Nerchinsk relief, and hid them in upstream inlets in winter;

sentences.zh: 馬有疲羸者，分發墨爾根、黑龍江飼秣，計持久。

translations.literal: horses that grew weary were sent to Merjen and Heilongjiang to be fed, planning a long siege.
translations.idiomatic: tired horses went to Merjen and Heilongjiang to recover—he planned a long siege.

sentences.zh: 上因荷蘭貢使以書諭俄羅斯察罕汗，答書請遣使畫界，先釋雅克薩圍，上允之，命撤圍。

translations.literal: Because the Dutch tribute envoy carried a letter instructing the Russian Tsagan Khan, the reply asked to send envoys to delimit the border and first lift the siege of Albazin; the emperor agreed and ordered the encirclement raised.
translations.idiomatic: A Dutch envoy's letter reached Russia's Tsagan Khan; Russia asked to delimit borders and lift the Albazin siege first—the emperor agreed and ordered the lines withdrawn.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，俄羅斯使臣費耀多囉等至尼布楚，命內大臣索額圖等往會，令發黑龍江兵千五百人為衛。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year the Russian envoys Feodor and others reached Nerchinsk; Inner Minister Songgotu and others were ordered to meet them, with fifteen hundred Heilongjiang troops sent as escort.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 28 Russian envoys led by Feodor came to Nerchinsk; Songgotu met them with fifteen hundred Heilongjiang guards.

sentences.zh: 尋議以大興安嶺及格爾必齊河為界，毀雅克薩城，徙其人去。

translations.literal: It was soon agreed to take the Greater Khingan and the Gorbitschi River as the border, destroy Albazin, and move its people away.
translations.idiomatic: The treaty set the Greater Khingan and Gorbitschi River as boundary, razed Albazin, and relocated its people.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，薩布素入覲，賜賚優渥，命坐內大臣班。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year Sabsu came to audience and was richly rewarded; he was ordered to sit in the inner-minister rank.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 29 he attended court, received lavish gifts, and was seated among inner ministers.

sentences.zh: 尋命總管索倫等部貢物，疏陳各部生計土俗採捕之事，擬為則例以上，上悉允行。

translations.literal: He was soon ordered to oversee tribute from the Solon and other departments; he memorialized on each people's livelihood, customs, and hunting and gathering, drafted regulations, and presented them upward; the emperor approved all.
translations.idiomatic: He was put in charge of Solon tribute, reported each tribe's economy and customs, drafted regulations, and won approval on every point.

sentences.zh: 三十一年，奏建齊齊哈爾及白都訥城，以科爾沁部獻進錫伯、卦爾察、達呼爾壯丁萬四千有奇分駐二城，編佐領，隸上三旗，並設防守尉、防禦等官。

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year he memorialized to build Qiqihar and Baidune cities, stationing more than fourteen thousand strong men of Xibe, Guwarcha, and Dahur presented by the Khorchin banners in the two cities, organizing assistant commands subordinate to the upper three banners, and establishing defense commandants and other officers.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 31 he proposed Qiqihar and Baidune, garrisoning fourteen thousand-odd Xibe, Guwarcha, and Dahur levies from Khorchin in both towns under new assistant commands of the upper three banners with defense officers.

sentences.zh: 噶爾丹入犯，疏陳進兵事宜，略言：「興安嶺北形勝地，以索約爾濟山為最。

translations.literal: When Galdan invaded he memorialized on the advance, stating in brief: "North of the Khingan the strongest ground is at Mount Suoyorji.
translations.idiomatic: When Galdan struck, he outlined the march: "North of the Khingan, Mount Suoyorji is the key ground.

sentences.zh: 已遣識路官兵自盛京、吉林、墨爾根審度至山遠近，分置驛站，其無水處，掘井以待。

translations.literal: Route-finding officers from Shengjing, Jilin, and Merjen have measured the distance to the mountain and placed post stations in stages; where there is no water, wells are dug in readiness.
translations.idiomatic: Scouts from Shengjing, Jilin, and Merjen have measured routes, set relay stations, and dug wells where water fails.

sentences.zh: 山之東北呼倫貝爾等處有警，與臣駐軍地近，即率墨爾根兵先進，吉林、盛京繼之；

translations.literal: If alarm comes from Hulun Buir and the northeast near my garrison, I will lead Merjen troops first and Jilin and Shengjing follow;
translations.idiomatic: If Hulun Buir alarms the northeast near my post, Merjen marches first, Jilin and Shengjing follow;

sentences.zh: 山之西烏勒輝等處有警，則盛京兵先進，臣率部下及吉林兵繼之：皆會於索約爾濟山。

translations.literal: if alarm comes from Ulehui and the west, Shengjing marches first and I with my command and Jilin follow—all to meet at Mount Suoyorji."
translations.idiomatic: if Ulehui alarms the west, Shengjing leads and I with Jilin follow—all converging on Suoyorji."

sentences.zh: 」上可其奏。

translations.literal: The emperor approved his memorial.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 三十五年，上親征噶爾丹，自獨石口出中路，大將軍費揚古自歸化城出西路，命薩布素扼其東路，督盛京、寧古塔、科爾沁兵，自索約爾濟山剋期進剿。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fifth year the emperor campaigned in person against Galdan, himself taking the center route from Dushikou while Grand General Feiyanggu left Guihua City on the western route; Sabsu was ordered to block the eastern route, directing Shengjing, Ningguta, and Khorchin troops to advance on schedule from Mount Suoyorji.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 35 the emperor marched on Galdan from Dushikou while Feiyanggu took the west from Guihua; Sabsu blocked the east with Shengjing, Ningguta, and Khorchin columns timed from Suoyorji.

sentences.zh: 四月，上次克魯倫河，噶爾丹西竄，為費揚古所敗。

translations.literal: In the fourth month the emperor reached the Kerulen River; Galdan fled west and was defeated by Feiyanggu.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month the emperor reached the Kerulen; Galdan fled west into Feiyanggu's defeat.

sentences.zh: 詔分薩布素所部兵五百人隸費揚古軍。

translations.literal: An edict detached five hundred of Sabsu's troops to Feiyanggu's army.
translations.idiomatic: Five hundred of Sabsu's men were assigned to Feiyanggu.

sentences.zh: 三十六年，召至京師，尋命回任。

translations.literal: In the thirty-sixth year he was summoned to the capital and soon ordered back to his post.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 36 he was called to Beijing, then sent back.

sentences.zh: 初，邊境有墨爾哲勒屯長，累世輸貢。

translations.literal: Earlier, on the frontier there was a Merenjeile company chief who for generations paid tribute.
translations.idiomatic: On the frontier a Merenjeile company chief had long paid tribute.

sentences.zh: 康熙初，屯長扎努喀布克托請率眾內移，寧古塔將軍巴海安輯於墨爾根，編四十佐領，號新滿洲。

translations.literal: Early in Kangxi the company chief Zanukabukto asked to lead his people inland; Ningguta General Bahai settled them at Merjen, organized forty assistant commands, and called them New Manchus.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Kangxi chief Zanukabukto asked to move inland; Bahai settled them at Merjen in forty companies styled New Manchus.

sentences.zh: 薩布素奏於墨爾根兩翼立學，設助教，選新滿洲及錫伯、索倫、達呼爾每佐領下幼童一，教習書義。

translations.literal: Sabsu memorialized to establish schools on both wings at Merjen, set assistant instructors, and choose one young boy from each assistant command of New Manchus, Xibe, Solon, and Dahur to study written meaning.
translations.idiomatic: Sabsu founded schools on both Merjen wings, appointed tutors, and enrolled one boy per company from New Manchus, Xibe, Solon, and Dahur to learn letters.

sentences.zh: 是為黑龍江建學之始。

translations.literal: This was the beginning of schooling in Heilongjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Thus began Heilongjiang's schools.

sentences.zh: 三十七年，上幸吉林，褒其勤勞，予一等阿達哈哈番世職，並御用冠服，於眾前宣諭賜之。

translations.literal: In the thirty-seventh year when the emperor visited Jilin he praised Sabsu's diligence, granted a first-class adaha fan hereditary rank and imperial court dress, and before the assembly proclaimed and bestowed them.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 37 at Jilin the emperor praised his service, gave him a first-class hereditary rank and imperial robes, and announced the gift before the host.

sentences.zh: 尋疏言黑龍江屯堡因災荒積欠米石，請俟年豐交倉。

translations.literal: He soon memorialized that Heilongjiang garrison farms, because of famine, owed accumulated grain and asked to deliver to the granary when the year was abundant.
translations.idiomatic: He reported Heilongjiang farms in arrears after famine and asked to repay the granaries in good years.

sentences.zh: 上以薩布素曾奏革任總督蔡毓榮經理十二堡，著有成效；

translations.literal: The emperor noted that Sabsu had once memorialized to remove Governor Cai Yurong from managing the twelve forts, with marked results;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor recalled Sabsu had urged removing Governor Cai Yurong from twelve forts with good results;

sentences.zh: 嗣因官堡荒棄，請停止屯種，將壯丁改歸驛站，存貯倉米，支放無餘，致駐防兵餉匱乏，責令回奏。

translations.literal: later, because official forts were abandoned to wasteland, he asked to stop farming, shift strong men to courier stations, store grain in the granary, disburse until none remained, causing garrison pay to run short—the emperor ordered him to answer.
translations.idiomatic: later he halted farming, shifted labor to posts, drained the granaries, and left garrison pay short—the emperor demanded an account.

sentences.zh: 薩布素具疏引罪，請以齊齊哈爾、墨爾根駐防兵每年輪派五百人往錫伯等處耕種官田，穫穀運齊齊哈爾交倉。

translations.literal: Sabsu submitted a confession, asking that five hundred garrison troops from Qiqihar and Merjen each year be rotated to farm state fields among the Xibe and others, harvest grain, and deliver it to Qiqihar granaries.
translations.idiomatic: Sabsu confessed and proposed rotating five hundred Qiqihar and Merjen garrisoners yearly to farm state land among the Xibe and ship grain to Qiqihar.

sentences.zh: 詔侍郎滿丕等往按，以薩布素將荒廢地妄報成效，並浮支穀石，應斬，命罷任，奪世職，在佐領上行走。

translations.literal: An edict sent Vice Minister Manpi and others to investigate; because Sabsu had falsely reported results on abandoned land and also overspent grain, death was proposed; he was ordered dismissed, stripped of hereditary rank, and to serve as assistant commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Manpi investigated; Sabsu had inflated yields on wasteland and overspent grain—the Board sought execution; he was dismissed, lost his title, and kept only an assistant command.

sentences.zh: 尋授散秩大臣。

translations.literal: He was soon made minister without portfolio.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made minister without portfolio.

sentences.zh: 三十九年，卒。

translations.literal: In the thirty-ninth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Kangxi 39.

sentences.zh: 乾隆間，敕修盛京通志，列名宦，且稱薩布素諳練明敏，得軍民心，其平羅剎及黑龍江興學，有文武幹濟才雲。

translations.literal: In the Qianlong period, by imperial order the Shengjing Gazetteer was compiled; he was listed among eminent officials, and it was said that Sabsu was skilled and keen, won the hearts of soldiers and people, that in pacifying the Russians and founding schools in Heilongjiang he had talent for both civil and military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Under Qianlong the Shengjing Gazetteer ranked him among eminent officials, praising his skill, soldiers' devotion, pacification of the Russians, and founding Heilongjiang schools—civil and military talent together.

sentences.zh: 瑪拉，那喇氏，滿洲鑲白旗人，尚書尼堪從子。

translations.literal: Ma La, of the Nara clan, was a Manchu of the Bordered White Banner and nephew of Minister Nikan.
translations.idiomatic: Ma La, Nara clan, Manchu Bordered White Banner, was Minister Nikan's nephew.

sentences.zh: 尼堪卒，無子，瑪拉與叔阿穆爾圖、阿錫圖及弟兆資分襲尼堪世職，瑪拉襲三等阿達哈哈番。

translations.literal: When Nikan died without a son, Ma La with his uncles Amurtu and Asitu and younger brother Zhaozi divided Nikan's hereditary office; Ma La inherited a third-class adaha fan.
translations.idiomatic: Nikan died childless; Ma La, uncles Amurtu and Asitu, and brother Zhaozi split the title—Ma La took a third-class adaha fan.

sentences.zh: 初任理籓院筆帖式。

translations.literal: He first served as a clerk in the Court of Colonial Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He began as a Colonial Affairs clerk.

sentences.zh: 順治五年，英親王阿濟格徵叛將薑瓖，圍大同，令瑪拉調蒙古兵以從。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Shunzhi Prince Ying Ajige campaigned against the rebel Jiang Xiang and besieged Datong; Ma La was ordered to mobilize Mongol troops to follow.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 5 Prince Ying Ajige besieged Datong against Jiang Xiang; Ma La mustered Mongol auxiliaries.

sentences.zh: 累遷理籓院副理事官。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to associate director of the Court of Colonial Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to associate director in the Colonial Affairs office.

sentences.zh: 康熙十四年，察哈爾布爾尼叛，聖祖命信郡王鄂扎帥師討之。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Kangxi the Chahar Borji rebelled; the Sacred Ancestor ordered Prince Xin Eje to command an army against him.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 14 Chahar Borji rebelled; the emperor sent Prince Xin Eje against him.

sentences.zh: 瑪拉自陳久任理籓院習知蒙古狀，原赴軍前效力，遂命與員外郎色棱赴科爾沁諸部調選兵馬協剿。

translations.literal: Ma La volunteered that long service in the Colonial Affairs office had made him familiar with Mongol conditions and he wished to serve at the front; he was therefore ordered with Director Seleng to the Khorchin banners to select horses and troops for the joint campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Ma La said long Colonial Affairs service taught him Mongolia and offered himself; he and Director Seleng were sent to Khorchin to levy horse and men.

sentences.zh: 師還，擢通政使，遷禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: When the army returned he was promoted to communications commissioner and transferred to vice minister of rites.
translations.idiomatic: After the campaign he became communications commissioner, then vice minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 十六年，擢工部尚書。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he was promoted to minister of works.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 16 he became minister of works.

sentences.zh: 偕內大臣喀岱往科爾沁諸外籓宣諭禁令。

translations.literal: Together with Inner Minister Kadai he went to the outer Khorchin banners to proclaim prohibitions.
translations.idiomatic: With Inner Minister Kadai he announced bans among the outer Khorchin banners.

sentences.zh: 瑪拉初受任，上誡以工部積弊，宜殫心釐剔。

translations.literal: When Ma La first took office the emperor admonished him that the Ministry of Works had accumulated abuses and he should devote his mind to correcting them.
translations.idiomatic: On taking office the emperor warned him to purge the Works Ministry's chronic abuses.

sentences.zh: 十九年，坐不能清積弊，議降五秩，詔從寬留任。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year, for failing to clear accumulated abuses, five ranks' demotion was proposed; an edict was lenient and he was retained.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 19 failure to reform brought a five-rank demotion proposal; the emperor kept him on.

sentences.zh: 復以饗殿器用修造疏忽，奪尚書，仍留世職。

translations.literal: Again, for negligent repair of vessels and utensils for the feast hall, he was stripped of the ministry but kept his hereditary rank.
translations.idiomatic: Negligence over feast-hall vessels cost him the ministry but not his title.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，上以俄羅斯數犯邊，擾及索倫、飛牙喀諸部，命集兵黑龍江，將進討，遣瑪拉往索倫儲軍實。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year, because Russia repeatedly violated the border and disturbed the Solon, Feiyaka, and other tribes, troops were mustered on the Amur for a coming campaign; Ma La was sent to Solon to store military supplies.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 22 Russia's border raids stirred Solon and Feiyaka; as troops gathered on the Amur, Ma La went to Solon to stock supplies.

sentences.zh: 尋疏言：「索倫總管博克所獲俄羅斯人及軍前招降者，皆迫於軍威，不宜久留索倫，應移之內地。

translations.literal: He soon memorialized: "Russians captured by Solon commander Boke and those who surrendered before the army were all compelled by military pressure and should not long remain in Solon; they should be moved inland."
translations.idiomatic: He urged moving inland Russians seized by Solon commander Boke or taken in battle—men held only by fear.

sentences.zh: 」詔允行。

translations.literal: An edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: The court agreed.

sentences.zh: 復言：「雅克薩、尼布楚二城久為羅剎所據，臣密诇雅克薩惟耕種自給，尼布楚歲捕貂與喀爾喀貿易資養贍。

translations.literal: He again said: "Albazin and Nerchinsk have long been held by the Russians; I secretly reconnoitered Albazin and found it lives only by its own farming; Nerchinsk each year hunts sable and trades with the Khalkha for subsistence.
translations.idiomatic: He added: "Albazin and Nerchinsk are long Russian—Albazin farms for itself; Nerchinsk lives on sable trade with the Khalkha.

sentences.zh: 請飭喀爾喀車臣汗禁所部與尼布楚貿易，並飭黑龍江將軍水陸並進，示將攻取雅克薩，因刈其田禾，則俄羅斯將不戰自困。

translations.literal: I ask that the Khalkha Tushiyetu Khan forbid his people to trade with Nerchinsk, and that the Heilongjiang general advance by land and water showing intent to take Albazin and cut their grain—then Russia will be trapped without fighting."
translations.idiomatic: Cut Nerchinsk trade via the Tushiyetu Khan, advance on Albazin by land and river, and mow their fields—Russia will collapse without battle."

sentences.zh: 」上然之，即以瑪拉所奏檄示喀爾喀。

translations.literal: The emperor approved and circulated Ma La's memorial to the Khalkha.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed and sent his memorial to the Khalkha.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，遣都統朋春等帥師往黑龍江議進兵，授瑪拉副都統銜，參贊軍務。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year Commander Peng Chun and others were sent to the Amur to discuss the advance; Ma La was given acting deputy lieutenant-general rank as staff adviser.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 24 Peng Chun went to the Amur to plan the advance; Ma La joined as acting deputy with staff rank.

sentences.zh: 遣蒙古兵三十诇雅克薩城，生擒羅剎七人，得城中設備及乞援各部狀。

translations.literal: Thirty Mongol troops were sent to scout Albazin; seven Russians were captured alive and the city's preparations and appeals for aid from various tribes were learned.
translations.idiomatic: Thirty Mongols scouted Albazin, took seven Russians alive, and learned the garrison's state and pleas for help.

sentences.zh: 是年夏，朋春等攻羅剎克之，逐其人。

translations.literal: That summer Peng Chun and others attacked the Russians and took the place, driving the people out.
translations.idiomatic: That summer Peng Chun stormed Albazin and expelled the garrison.

sentences.zh: 瑪拉在事有功。

translations.literal: Ma La had merit in the affair.
translations.idiomatic: Ma La earned credit in the campaign.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，黑龍江佐領鄂色以耕牛多斃，農器損壞，奏請儲備，命瑪拉往黑龍江督理農務。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year Heilongjiang assistant commandant Ese, because many plow oxen died and farm tools were damaged, memorialized for reserves; Ma La was ordered to Heilongjiang to supervise agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 25 assistant commandant Ese reported dead oxen and broken tools; Ma La was sent to oversee farming.

sentences.zh: 諭曰：「農事關軍餉，令嚴督合力播種。

translations.literal: He was instructed: "Agriculture bears on army provisions; order strict supervision for united sowing."
translations.idiomatic: He was told: "Farms feed the army—supervise planting closely."

sentences.zh: 」值歲豐，收穫甚稔。

translations.literal: The year was abundant and the harvest very full.
translations.idiomatic: Harvest that year was abundant.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，授護軍統領。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year he was made guards commander.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 27 he became guards commander.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，噶爾丹侵掠喀爾喀，命瑪拉偕都統額赫納、前鋒統領碩鼐等率兵往討之，賜內廝馬以行。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year, when Galdan raided the Khalkha, Ma La was ordered with Commander Ehena, Vanguard Commander Shuonai, and others to lead troops against him and was granted an imperial stable horse for the journey.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 29, as Galdan raided the Khalkha, Ma La marched with Ehena and Shuonai and received an imperial horse.

sentences.zh: 未幾，噶爾丹掠烏珠穆沁，命裕親王福全等分統大軍出塞擊之，噶爾丹敗遁。

translations.literal: Before long Galdan raided Ujimchin; Prince Fuquan and others were ordered to lead great armies beyond the passes to strike him, and Galdan was defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Galdan struck Ujimchin; Prince Fuquan drove him beyond the passes in defeat.

sentences.zh: 師旋，三十年，復來犯，至阿爾哈賚，無所掠而遁。

translations.literal: When the army returned, in the thirtieth year he came again, reaching Arhabsan, found nothing to plunder, and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 30 he returned to Arhabsan, found no booty, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 時土謝圖汗、車臣汗率所部來歸，上幸塞外撫輯，瑪拉扈從。

translations.literal: At that time the Tushiyetu and Tsetsen khans led their people to submit; the emperor went beyond the passes to comfort them and Ma La attended.
translations.idiomatic: As the Tushiyetu and Tsetsen khans submitted, the emperor toured the frontier and Ma La attended.

sentences.zh: 旋命偕都統瓦岱等率兵赴圖拉偵噶爾丹，抵克魯倫河，聞其遠竄，乃還。

translations.literal: He was soon ordered with Commander Wadai and others to lead troops to Tula to scout Galdan; reaching the Kerulen they heard he had fled far and returned.
translations.idiomatic: He and Wadai were sent to scout Tula, reached the Kerulen, heard Galdan had fled, and turned back.

sentences.zh: 授西安將軍。

translations.literal: He was appointed Xi'an general.
translations.idiomatic: He became Xi'an general.

sentences.zh: 三十二年，準噶爾和碩特部台吉巴圖爾額爾克濟農來降，上以其人未可信，命瑪拉徙入內地，毋令复逸。

translations.literal: In the thirty-second year the Khoshut taiji Batur Erkejin of Dzungaria came to surrender; the emperor, deeming him untrustworthy, ordered Ma La to move him inland and not let him escape again.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 32 Khoshut taiji Batur Erkejin of Dzungaria surrendered; distrusting him, the emperor told Ma La to resettle him inland.

sentences.zh: 瑪拉疏言：「巴圖爾額爾克濟農率所屬二千餘口，窮乏來歸，揆其情狀，當不復逸。

translations.literal: Ma La memorialized: "Batur Erkejin leads more than two thousand followers in destitution to submit; judging their situation, they will not flee again."
translations.idiomatic: Ma La judged two thousand-odd destitute followers would not flee again.

sentences.zh: 」遂遣官護送，併其子台吉雲木春來朝，優賚遣之。

translations.literal: Officials were sent to escort them, and his son the taiji Yunmuchun also came to court and was generously rewarded and sent away.
translations.idiomatic: Escorts were sent; his son Yunmuchun attended court, was rewarded, and dismissed.

sentences.zh: 未幾，瑪拉卒於官，賜祭葬，諡敏恪。

translations.literal: Before long Ma La died in office; funeral rites were granted and the posthumous name Minke was given.
translations.idiomatic: He soon died in office with funeral honors and posthumous name Minke.

sentences.zh: 論曰：俄羅斯之為羅剎，譯言緩急異耳，非必東部別有是名也。

translations.literal: The commentary says: That Russia is called Luocha is only a difference of translation in speed of speech, not necessarily that the east has another name.
translations.idiomatic: The commentary notes: "Luocha" for Russia is mere transliteration—not a separate eastern people.

sentences.zh: 初遣兵诇敵，郎坦主其事；

translations.literal: When troops were first sent to reconnoiter the enemy, Lang Tan directed the affair;
translations.idiomatic: Lang Tan led the first reconnaissance;

sentences.zh: 取雅克薩城，朋春、薩布素迭為將，而郎坦與瑪拉實佐之。

translations.literal: in taking Albazin, Peng Chun and Sabsu served as commanders in turn, while Lang Tan and Ma La truly assisted.
translations.idiomatic: Peng Chun and Sabsu commanded the captures, with Lang Tan and Ma La as the chief aides.

sentences.zh: 尼布楚盟定，開市庫倫，是為我國與他國定約互市之始。

translations.literal: After the Nerchinsk treaty, trade was opened at Khuree—this was the beginning of our state's treaties and mutual trade with other countries.
translations.idiomatic: After Nerchinsk, Khuree trade opened—the first treaty market with a foreign power.

sentences.zh: 用兵當期必克，我苟草率，彼益猖狂，聖祖諭薩布素數言，得馭夷之要矣。

translations.literal: In war one must time for certain victory; if we are rash they grow still bolder—the Sacred Ancestor's several instructions to Sabsu grasp the essentials of controlling barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: War demands sure victory; rashness only emboldens foes—the emperor's words to Sabsu state the art of handling frontier powers.
